sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Legal Accounting Defense for International Anti-Dumping Inquiries

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement with Chile, Mexico and Peru

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 1121 of 2006 (AML/CFT framework), Law 526 of 1999 (financial intelligence unit), Law 1762 of 2015 (anti-contraband and money laundering), Law 1778 of 2016 (anti-corruption), Decree 1009 of 2023 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUB), DIAN Resolution 164 of 2021 (RUB procedures), and Superintendence of Companies External Circular 100-0000001 of 2021 (SAGRILAFT).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate existence certificate of the foreign direct parent entity (Certificado de Existencia y Representación)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or Chamber of Commerce of the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the origin state is not party to the Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or government-issued identity document of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport or identity authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification followed by Hague Apostille on the notarial certificate (or consular legalization when inapplicable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for the incorporation of the S.A.S. and registration before the Cámara de Comercio
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the jurisdiction of origin of the grantor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization in non-Apostille jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming banking history and source of funds of the shareholders and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent or relationship bank of the shareholder / UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the authenticated bank signature; consular legalization for non-Apostille jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form under Colombian RUB requirements, signed under oath
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Colombian notary and/or the S.A.S. legal representative after incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Colombia; foreign signatures must be notarized and then authenticated by Hague Apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and UBOs must be screened against OFAC SDN, the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU sanctions, and Colombian domestic lists maintained by DIAN, Procuraduría, and the Superintendence of Companies. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined under Law 1121 of 2006, including government officials, diplomatic and military officers, state-owned enterprise executives, and their close relatives. The screening process must include source-of-funds verification and continuous monitoring; standing operating procedure requires re-screening at least every six months under the SAGRILAFT model.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial y Social, operated through the local Cámara de Comercio virtual portal (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Spanish; Latin characters with Spanish diacritical marks are permitted. The name must include a corporate type abbreviation, most commonly 'S.A.S.', 'S.A.' or 'Ltda.' as applicable. Foreign words are acceptable only if transliterated into the Latin alphabet, not generic, and sufficiently distinctive to avoid confusion. All constitutional and public-registry documents must be prepared in Spanish; foreign-supplied documents must be translated by a certified translator.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a reconsideration request with the same Cámara de Comercio within five business days. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may file a formal objection before the Superintendencia de Sociedades, attaching evidence of prior trademark rights or a certificate showing that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. The objection must be accompanied by the original name-search certificate and payment of the administrative fee. If the name is rejected on grounds of being generic, misleading, or contrary to public order, a new name must be presented; the name reservation may in practice be renewed for one additional 30-day period where no conflicting rights arise.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with limitations for a low-risk professional consulting S.A.S. A virtual office may satisfy the registered-office requirement for service of process and commercial registration, provided that the company designates a Colombian domicile and appoints a statutory agent reasonably available to receive notices. In practice, DIAN requires an actual operational address for tax residency and invoicing purposes, and the SAGRILAFT risk-management framework expects physical access to records and key personnel; therefore a hybrid model of a virtual administrative office plus a physical professional address is recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 25% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection during the first fiscal year, given the 'low-risk' ISIC 7490 professional-services classification and the authority of the Cámara de Comercio, DIAN, and the Superintendence of Companies to conduct supervisory visits; probability decreases with a formal registered office and complete statutory bookkeeping.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization fees for private incorporation documents
Apostille and legalization of foreign corporate documents (set of up to five documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the document origin country; for Colombian-issued documents, Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registry filing and RUB pre-registration professional preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN (filing itself is gratuitous) plus accredited corporate counsel/accountant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: DIAN fee: zero; professional preparation: prevailing market benchmark flat fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial AML/CFT risk assessment and PEP/sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed compliance provider or corporate law firm

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAS incorporation legal drafting (bylaws, shareholders' resolutions, compliance manual, anti-dumping trade-defense service engagement templates)
Commercial registry registration fee (liquidated based on registered capital)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio and Superintendence of Companies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on registered capital and number of registration acts

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory registered agent and physical registered-office address service for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent service provider in Colombia

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation and linguistic review of foreign-origin documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per-page or flat fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971) arts. 110, 112, 353-373, and Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015 Libro 2.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio principal (Registro Único Empresarial – RUES), under supervision of Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation deed with notarial authentication); Escritura Pública required when real property is contributed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Ley 1258 de 2008; capital is freely determined by the shareholders. Subscribed shares must be paid within two (2) years from incorporation; no escrow account is mandated for cash contributions, but contributions in kind must be itemized, valued, and delivered as recorded in the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE INAUGURAL MEETING OF SHAREHOLDERS OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S.: The sole shareholder, acting under Ley 1258 de 2008, resolves: (1) subscription and payment of all issued shares is ratified, constituting the paid-up capital; (2) the registered office and fiscal domicile are adopted at the address given in the incorporation deed; (3) [Name] is appointed Representante Legal and [Name] as Secretary, with full powers to represent the company before public registries and financial institutions; (4) the officers are authorized to file the incorporation documents with the Cámara de Comercio, obtain the NIT/RUT from DIAN, and execute banking and labor registrations; (5) all prior constitutive acts are approved. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability search and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Único Empresarial (RUES), Cámara de Comercio del domicilio principal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Certificado de Homologación de Nombre through the RUES online portal or the Chamber's counter. Provide up to five proposed corporate names. If available, the name is reserved for thirty (30) calendar days pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Application form for name homologation
Copy of shareholders' national ID or passport
Proof of payment of the search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or identical to an existing trademark, file a new homologation request with alternative names; no material delay expected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarial authentication of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (autenticación de firmas) for private document
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución under Ley 1258 de 2008, including the company name, shareholder details, registered office, share classes, paid-in capital schedule, and governance terms. All shareholder signatures must be authenticated before a notary. If real property is contributed, execute a public deed (Escritura Pública) before a notary of the property's location.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation document
Certified name homologation certificate
Valid government-issued ID of each shareholder
Notarial authentication form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, correct the deed and re-authenticate; minor registry deficiencies can be cured through an aclaratory instrument (instrumento aclaratorio).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration and issuance of certificate of existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio principal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authenticated incorporation deed, pay the registration tariff and recursos de inscripción, and complete the single commercial registration form (Formulario RUES). The Chamber will register the company, authorize the corporate books, and issue the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
required_dossiers: Authenticated incorporation document
Completed RUES registration form
Name homologation certificate
Proof of registered office (lease or letter of authorization)
Original ID of the appointed Representante Legal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried under article 112 of the Código de Comercio, submit rectifications within thirty (30) working days; the registry will issue the certificate after cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with DIAN (RUT/NIT) and electronic signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) and obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) through the DIAN online portal (DIAN Resolución 000055 de 2023). Select the applicable tax regime (ordinary, IVA responsible or not, and relevant industry codes). Activate the electronic invoicing system and obtain the electronic signature (firma electrónica).
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Valid ID of the Representante Legal and legal representative's authorization documentary evidence
Proof of registered office address
Corporate email and bank account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or frozen, file an 'actualización del RUT' with corrected data and supporting documents; escalation to DIAN service channel for expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social security enrollment, ARL registration, and corporate bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed ARL (e.g., Positiva), social security operators, and commercial bank of choice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the Sistema General de Seguridad Social (health, pension, labor risks). Select and contract an Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL) for occupational risk coverage. Open a corporate checking account in the company's name, presenting the certificate of existence and shareholder resolutions.
required_dossiers: NIT/RUT certificate
Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Valid ID of representatives and shareholders
Registered office lease agreement with property tax certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration data is inconsistent, correct through the payroll and social security operator portals; bank may request additional background checks, remedy by providing supplementary notarial certifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral registry filing with the foreign trade authority and operational commencement notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Comercio, Industria y Turismo (MinCIT) – Dirección de Comercio Exterior
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a notice of specialized professional services in international trade defense under Decreto 1074 de 2015, confirming the company's capacity to advise Colombian exporters in anti-dumping investigations. Register the legal counsel's professional credentials (Tarjeta Profesional de Abogado) and obtain any applicable certificate of operational capacity for cross-border consulting services.
required_dossiers: RUT and NIT certification
Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Professional license of the responsible counsel
Description of services and conflict-of-interest policy
EIA registration certificate if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MinCIT issues a requerimiento de información, answer within fifteen (15) working days; failure to cure results in re-filing, and the new application is prioritized upon presentation of the missing documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio, Industria y Turismo (MinCIT) – Dirección de Regulación de Comercio Exterior
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro de Operador de Servicios de Defensa Comercial y Consultoría en Comercio Exterior (under Decree 1074 de 2015)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category Registration – Low-Impact Office-Based Professional Services; no full EIA required given zero industrial effluents or process emissions; limited municipal environmental registration for solid waste and office discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Resolution 0631 de 2015 for conventional pollutants in wastewater discharged to municipal sewers; Resolution 0909 de 2008 for indoor and boundary noise levels; special handling and recycling of e-waste under Resolution 1512 de 2010 (RAEE regime); municipal solid waste disposal through accredited collectors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos for the registered office; structural load and occupancy inspection by the municipal planning authority confirming office-use compliance; workplace safety and health workplace clearance registered with the contracted ARL; compliance with minimum occupational hygiene standards under Resolution 2400 de 1979.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official electronic portal: https://www.dian.gov.co and DIAN's 'Sede Electrónica' taxpayer virtual center for RUT application, NIT issuance, electronic invoicing validation, and export declaration management.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-domiciled foreign entity must first obtain a DIAN-issued electronic signature ('firma electrónica') for online authentication, then register in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) to obtain or update a Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT). For an Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) with non-resident shareholders, the registration is performed by the legal representative (or appointed domiciliary agent) through DIAN's RUT en línea platform, submitting apostilled and Spanish-translated constitutional documents, proof of legal existence in the home jurisdiction, a notarized power of attorney evidencing the representative's appointment, and, where applicable, a Colombian branch or agency license issued by the Superintendencia de Sociedades. After validation of RUT data, DIAN issues a single NIT number that simultaneously covers entity status, VAT, income tax, and customs/foreign trade registration obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident Colombian S.A.S. corporations are separate taxpayers subject to corporate income tax on their worldwide income; no pass-through regime applies). For a foreign parent with a Colombian permanent establishment through an S.A.S. branch context, the territorial scope is limited to Colombia-source income, and the S.A.S. itself remains the VAT and customs taxable person. Tax-Exempt_Zone benefits are not automatic and require specific Zona Franca registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' or elective hybrid classification mechanism. A Colombian S.A.S. may however elect: (i) the 'Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE)' under Articles 903-915 of the Estatuto Tributario for eligible entities below the 100,000 UVT gross revenue threshold; (ii) consolidated or group taxation election for entities forming a business group ('grupo empresarial'); (iii) the option to appear before DIAN for permanent or bimonthly export VAT refunds under Decreto 1625 de 2016; (iv) Zona Franca developer or user regime elections, if applicable; and (v) the ancillary election to request extension of the foreign-exchange repatriation deadline before Banco de la República. Hybrid mismatch rules under Law 2010 of 2019 are mandatory anti-avoidance provisions and are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Agregado (IVA) / VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general monetary turnover threshold triggering IVA registration for S.A.S. entities: any legal person habitually supplying taxable goods or services in Colombia must register in the RUT and take a category as IVA responsible ('responsable del IVA'). The 'Régimen Simplificado' small-trader exception is available only to natural persons/artisans and does not apply to an S.A.S.; however, for reference, simplified taxpayers are limited to gross income below 3,500 UVT (approx. COP 170 million per year) and other statutory conditions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-responsible entities must issue invoices through DIAN's mandatory electronic invoicing system ('Facturación Electrónica'). The invoice XML must be transmitted in real time to DIAN's validation platform, either by an authorized 'Proveedor Tecnológico' or through DIAN's free software application, before the invoice is legally delivered. Once validated, each invoice is assigned either a 'Código Único de Factura Electrónica (CUFE)' for standard sales invoices or a 'Código Único de Documento Soporte (CUDS)' for purchase/support documents. The generated PDF or XML must carry a QR code linking to DIAN repositories, the issuer's digital certificate, and the DIAN electronic stamp. Export invoices and supporting declarations (Declaración de Exportación / DEX) are also transmitted through the same system and must match the customs exit records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports are eligible for the 0% VAT rate when the exporter is an IVA-responsible entity, the goods permanently leave Colombian customs territory under an accepted DEX, and documentary proof of physical exit and foreign payment is maintained. Export services, including legal and trade-defense consulting, qualify for 0% VAT only if the beneficiary is a non-domiciled entity, the service is used exclusively abroad, the service is rendered from Colombia but not connected to the production or marketing of taxable goods within Colombia, and the foreign client receives formal invoices plus service certificates. Inbound payments must be channeled through the Colombian foreign-exchange market, and a written contract describing the offshore use must be kept.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación / DEX) accepted by DIAN
Bill of Lading (ocean transport) or Air Waybill (air cargo) evidencing physical exit of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Canalización de Divisas) issued by an authorized Colombian foreign-exchange intermediary
Final commercial invoice and packing list
Export contract or foreign purchase order containing Incoterms and payment terms
Certificate of origin and any applicable export permit or license (sanitary, environmental, or customs broker authorization)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may audit any export operation where the DEX, shipping documents, service contract, or foreign-exchange proceeds are missing, inconsistent, or backdated. If zero-rating is disallowed, DIAN will retroactively assess the unpaid 19% IVA with monthly default interest and applies the 'sanción por inexactitud' under Article 647 of the Estatuto Tributario, generally equal to 160% of the greater amount of tax due or refund obtained. Improperly obtained export VAT refunds are clawed back with retroactive effect together with penalties of up to 20% of the refunded amount, and the taxpayer may be suspended from operating or invoicing for up to ten days. Where fraud or criminal intent is shown, DIAN and the Fiscalía General de la Nación may bring charges under Articles 402 and 403 of the Código Penal, carrying imprisonment, disqualification, and fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia), with foreign exchange administration partially delegated to the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) for enforcement and customs-related control; the Junta Directiva del Banco de la República issues foreign exchange regulations under Decree 1068 of 2015.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is generally convertible for current account operations, including payments for services, royalties, and profit remittances, subject to mandatory foreign exchange channeling through authorized intermediaries and registration in the Declaración de Cambio system. Capital account operations, including foreign direct investment, require prior registration with Banco de la República through a local authorized intermediary using Form 5 (Declaración de Cambio por Inversiones Internacionales). Profit and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted once the underlying investment is registered, corporate tax clearances (e.g., the parafiscal and tax compliance certificate issued by DIAN) are obtained, and the remittance is channeled through the exchange market. Bucket operations, offshore settlement outside the regulated exchange market, and invoicing practises that avoid exchange channeling constitute strict violations under Colombian foreign exchange regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters of goods and services must channel foreign currency proceeds through the Colombian foreign exchange market via authorized intermediaries (banks or financial corporations) within the statutory timelines: goods exports must be collected and channeled within six months from the date of the export declaration (declaración de exportación), and service exports must be collected and channeled within five months from the maturing or accrual date of the corresponding operation, as established in Banco de la República External Regulations and Decree 1068 of 2015, Book 3. There is no mandatory full surrender ratio; the exporter may keep foreign currency in a foreign currency deposit account in a local authorized bank, but the initial receipt and channeling must occur through the intermediario del mercado cambiario. Failure to channel export proceeds within the term triggers corrective declarations, fines, and potential anti-money-laundering scrutiny.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs and neobanks not licensed by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia have limited legal viability for receiving Colombian-source trade or service export revenue. Any cross-border virtual account that seeks to replace mandated exchange market channeling is non-compliant. Locally regulated financial technology companies (e.g., authorized Sociedades Especializadas en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos – SEDPEs) and banking-as-a-service platforms integrated with tier-1 banks are viable for treasury operations, but they cannot replace the intermediario del mercado cambiario for FX channeling. Offshore EMIs may be used solely as auxiliary payment rails for low-value operational expenses, provided all export and capital receipts are separately channelled through a Colombian authorized intermediary.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Colombian S.A.S. with non-resident directors, physical presence of all directors is generally not mandatory for corporate account opening; however, the legal representative or designated authorized agent must provide biometric identification and a certified copy of the notarized bylaws (certificado de existencia y representación legal) issued by the Cámara de Comercio within the last 30 days. Non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners must provide passport copies, proof of address, and, where required, apostilled powers of attorney. Some tier-1 banks, particularly in the 'Low' viability categories, may demand an in-person interview of the legal representative at a Colombian branch. Remote opening is possible for non-listed low-risk professional services entities, subject to enhanced video KYC, biometric liveness checks, and the completion of a corporate due diligence questionnaire signed by the legal representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners and foreign incorporated parent companies without clear economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized corporate registry extracts from the home jurisdiction, apostilled or legalized; audited financial statements for the last 2 years; tax residence certificates; detailed organisational chart showing all UBOs; and a signed declaration of economic substance describing employees, office premises, business purpose, and revenue sources.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client base concentrated in politically exposed persons (PEPs) or entities in jurisdictions considered high-risk (FATF watchlist)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP screening questionnaire, copies of professional licences of the ultimate client, source-of-funds documentation (independent KYC file), and a written anti-money-laundering risk assessment prepared by an external compliance consultant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High proportion of inbound transfers from unrelated third parties for legal-services invoices (antidumping defense agreements)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copies of signed service contracts, itemized invoices, documentary evidence of the underlying trade-defense proceedings (e.g., official anti-dumping case docket numbers), and payment confirmations matching the invoiced party; plus a sworn statement explaining the commercial rationale for any third-party payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of opaque trusts or private foundation structures as shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trust deed or foundation charter, register of settlors, protectors, and final beneficiaries; notarized certifications from the fiduciary or foundation board; and an independent legal opinion confirming the economic substance of the structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment into a Colombian S.A.S. must be routed through an authorized foreign exchange intermediary (a Colombian commercial bank) using the Declaración de Cambio for foreign investment (Form 5). The investor or the company must register the investment with Banco de la República within the information system before or after the transfer, as applicable. Wire instructions must include the CITI (Código de Inversión Territorial e Internacional) or the investor identification code, the foreign investment registration code (when available), and a payment reference stating 'Registro de inversión internacional bajo Decreto 1068 de 2015'. The incoming wire must be in USD, EUR, or COP, and the receiving bank will issue a declaración de cambio that simultaneously records the capital injection. The account should be a dedicated operational or capital escrow account, and the 'concepto cambiario' must be coded as 'Inversión directa en el exterior – establecimiento permanente – suplemento de capital' or equivalent for equity contributions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for anti-dumping defense services (e.g., payments to foreign legal counsel, economic consultants, expert witnesses, and official filing fees) must be executed via SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers, or through documentary commercial letters of credit (UCP600) when the counterparty requires restricted or sight-payment modalities. All outbound service payments require a Declaración de Cambio Form 6 (servicios) submitted through an authorized intermediary, with supporting invoices, contracts, and tax clearance from DIAN confirming no outstanding tax or customs liabilities. The company may hold USD-denominated or EUR-denominated accounts in a local authorized bank to reduce conversion cost, but any payment to a non-resident must be reported to the exchange market within the applicable three-day correction window. For larger trade settlements, MT202 for beneficiary bank transfers may be used alongside the underlying MT103, and beneficiary bank costs must be pre-agreed to avoid shortfalls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts (Forwards de tasa de cambio) between the S.A.S. and a local authorized intermediary, subject to underlying exchange exposure and Banco de la República regulations

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to COP, when contracted with a supervised local financial institution onshore or a counterparty acceptable to Banco de la República, provided hedge documentation demonstrates a real commercial exposure
Currency swaps (swap de divisas) with local authorized banks for managing multi-currency cash flows
Plain-vanilla FX options (call/put options on COP/USD) and cross-currency swaps with regulated financial institutions for hedging receivables/payables up to 12 months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the mercantile registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil) — the S.A.S. corporate registration, updated statement of assets/liabilities, RUT certificate and UBO information filed with the RUES
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered seat (e.g., Bogotá D.C. or Medellín); coordinated through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March of each year for the calendar year preceding the renewal (no Grace period; deadline is peremptory)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic surcharge of 1.5% per calendar month (or fraction) on the renewal tariff up to 100% of the fee; non-renewal for two consecutive years causes administrative cancellation of the mercantile registration (strike-off) with loss of reliable legal standing toward third parties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved annual financial statements (estados financieros – IFRS/NIIF), shareholder-approved, together with the management report and, if applicable, the revisor fiscal opinion, registered for publicity with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (RUES recordal); accessible to the Superintendencia de Sociedades for oversight purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting of the S.A.S. must approve accounts within three months after 31 December (by 31 March); financial statements are annexed to the mercantile renewal filed on the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The renewal remains incomplete and the registration cannot be authenticated; legal-representative liability for losses; DIAN may apply Article 651 penalties on inaccurate financial information; dividends paid on unaudited accounts remain challengeable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax-information return (información exógena) and statutory transfer-pricing documentation for cross-border services supplied in connection with anti-dumping trade-defense consultancies (where related parties are involved)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) — electronic submission through the MUISCA portal with digital certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window in the first half of each year (typically mid-February through mid-April); exact final date depends on the last two digits of the NIT per the official DIAN tax calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Article 651 ET for omission or defects up to 5% of the gross annual income (or 1% for formal defects); adverse effects on the good-taxpayer status required for foreign-trade and investment formalities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of final beneficiaries (beneficiario final/UBO) in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT), including registration of any share transfers carried out during the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (RUT electronic updating service, with digital certificate and legal-representative validation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation together with the 31 March renewal cycle; share transfers must be entered in the share register immediately and the RUT/UBO schedule updated within one month after the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: DIAN penalties under Article 651 ET (up to 5% of gross annual income) for inaccurate or omitted beneficiary information; inaccuracies may trigger the anti-tax-evasion re-characterization regime under Law 2010 of 2019 and loss of transparency good-faith status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (revisor fiscal) is mandatory when at the prior 31 December: (a) total assets reach 5,000 SMMLV (COP 6.5 billion for fiscal year 2024; ca. USD 1.6 million); (b) gross annual income reaches 3,000 SMMLV (COP 3.9 billion; ca. USD 1.0 million); or (c) the S.A.S. heads a business group or is under permanent control of the Superintendencia de Sociedades. Below these thresholds, a revisor fiscal is voluntary and the legal representative certifies the financial statements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NIIF (IFRS) as adopted in Colombia pursuant to Law 1314/2009 and regulatory Decrees 2420 and 2496/2015: Group 1 = full IFRS, Group 2 = IFRS for SMEs, Group 3 = micro-entity standard; a professional-services S.A.S. typically applies Group 2. Financial statements are presented in COP; books and supporting vouchers are retained 10 years under Código de Comercio Article 63, with tax records additionally kept for the period of firmeza (at least 5 years)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 2010/2019 and DIAN Resolution 000164/2024, the S.A.S. must identify each natural person holding, directly or indirectly, 5% or more of the share capital or exercising control/profit entitlements, and file an annual confirmation of the UBO schedule through the RUT module. The legal representative attests the schedule; every transfer of shares is recorded in the share register with effective date and the UBO schedule is updated within one month; the annual confirmation closes on the prior 31 December and is filed together with the mercantile renewal on 31 March
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas) – shares, transfers, usufruct and pledges
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva, if a board exists; legal-representative appointments recorded with the Cámara de Comercio)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Asamblea de Accionistas)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The effective Colombian corporate income tax rate is generally 35%. Certain deductions can lower the effective burden: a 25% income tax deduction for qualifying investments in science, technology and innovation (STI) projects, a 50% wage deduction under Law 1780/2016 for qualifying new employees, and VAT zero-rating for exported professional consulting services. The Colombia Holding Company (CHC) regime may also exempt foreign-source dividends if the SAS qualifies as a CHC. The anti-dumping trade defense consulting activity does not typically fall within the temporary 'economia naranja' creative-industries exemption unless expressly registered and approved by the competent committee.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios de personas jurídicas y asimiladas) filed through the DIAN Muisca electronic filing system (Síntesis portal) using the taxpayer's digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return for the preceding calendar year is due in April of the following year. The exact filing date is assigned by the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT (tax identification number) pursuant to the annual DIAN calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from anti-dumping defense consulting, legal advisory, economic analysis, and related professional services invoiced during the taxable year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Colombian resident SAS, report all worldwide revenue. For a non-resident taxpayer that is subject to Colombian taxation through a permanent establishment, report only Colombian-source income attributable to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos no constitutivos de renta (non-taxable income): dividends received from Colombian resident companies, legally exempt income, and amounts excluded under specific statutory provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident with a Colombian PE may exclude only income that is legally exempt under Colombian law or under an applicable DTA. Foreign dividends received by a resident SAS are generally taxable unless the CHC regime applies; consult the CHC election requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Devoluciones, rebajas y descuentos (returns, rebates and discounts): contractual refunds, trade discounts and billing adjustments granted to clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the same values in the books of the Colombian PAYROLL or PE. Reimbursements of third-party costs received from foreign clients must be shown only if they represent actual gross income to the SAS; pure pass-through payments with no margin must be documented as agency or mandate arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costos de venta y prestación de servicios (direct costs of providing services): salaries of attorneys, economists, expert witnesses, data licensing for trade analytics, and external consultant fees engaged specifically for anti-dumping defense mandates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Direct costs are deductible only when they are necessary, proportionate and properly evidenced. In a foreign-owned SAS, payments to related offshore service providers must satisfy the arm's length condition and should be backed by a full intercompany services agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gastos operacionales (operating expenses): office rent, utilities, software licences, professional subscriptions, business development costs, AML compliance upkeep, insurance and administrative payroll.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Colombian PE of a foreign company, operating expenses are limited to those incurred for the PE in Colombia. Head office charges and management fees are deductible only if the foreign head office proves actual services and an arm's length allocation, supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta líquida gravable (net taxable income): taxable income after permitted cost and expense deductions, tax depreciation, amortization, and the offset of unexpired tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net taxable income is computed on Colombian-source revenue attributable to the taxpayer or PE. Losses of a foreign head office cannot be offset against Colombian PE income except under DTA business profits rules and Colombian loss-recognition limitations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto de renta (corporate income tax) computed at the statutory 35% rate on Box 47 net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 35% rate applies to the Colombian PE taxable income of a non-resident entity, except where a DTA restricts the taxable base or rate. No treaty reduction is available for income taxed as a permanent establishment unless the treaty articles so provide.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Retenciones, anticipos y créditos tributarios (withholdings, prepayments and tax credits): tax withheld by clients, advance payments of income tax, VAT on non-deductible purchases, and foreign taxes paid on income recognized in Colombia.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits may be claimed by the Colombian resident SAS for withholding taxes imposed by foreign jurisdictions on its trade-defense consulting fees, subject to the limitation rules of the Colombian Tax Code. A non-resident PE in Colombia cannot credit foreign taxes unrelated to its Colombian income; treaty with low-tax countries must be reviewed to exclude double counting.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a surcharge of 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of month, capped at 100% of the tax payable. If no tax is due, a fixed sanction of 5 to 10 UVT (about COP 500,000 to COP 1,000,000) applies for late filing. Late payment of income tax attracts moratory interest at the bank lending rate plus 8%. Failure to present a return when legally obligated is sanctioned with a fine of up to 20% of the tax determined; a false or inexact return may result in a fine of 50% to 100% of the understated amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividends paid to non-resident beneficiaries when the profits distributed were previously taxed at the 35% corporate income tax rate. If profits originated from exempt or non-taxed income, the dividend becomes subject to final tax at the rate of 33% as a non-qualified distribution. Resident individual shareholders are additionally taxed at 7.5% on annual dividends above 300 UVT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from a double tax agreement, the foreign shareholder or beneficiary must provide the Colombian withholding agent with an original Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by its tax authority, accompanied by a formal written treaty-relief claim. The withholding agent must upload the certificate and supporting documents to the DIAN Muisca portal and retain them for five years. If the treaty rate is not applied at source because the TRC is submitted late, the foreign beneficiary may apply for a refund from DIAN through the 'devolución y compensación' procedure within four years from the payment date. Additional documentation may be required for fiscally transparent entities and for dividends, interest, and royalties payments under specific DTA articles.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties (IP licenses and know-how) paid to foreign beneficiaries are subject to a domestic withholding tax rate of 33%; under DTAs the rate is generally reduced to 10% or 15% depending on the asset and the treaty. Interest on cross-border debt is subject to a domestic withholding tax rate of 15%; under DTAs the rate is typically reduced to 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File preparation applies when the taxpayer's gross income or total gross assets in the preceding taxable year equal or exceed COP 100,000,000,000 (approximately USD 25 million). In addition, taxpayers with related-party cross-border transactions exceeding COP 50,000,000,000 must file the Transfer Pricing Informative Return (Form 120). The thresholds are annually adjusted for inflation by DIAN.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime analogous to the UAE. However, the SAS must maintain real economic substance in Colombia to prevent adverse transfer pricing adjustments, the application of the Colombian General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR, Article 658-3 of the Tax Code), and the Controlled Foreign Corporation (CFC) rules (Article 882 of the Tax Code). Substance indicators include a physical office in Colombia, full-time qualified employees, board meetings held in Colombia, execution of contracts and invoices from Colombian territory, and commercial risk assumed by the SAS. Absence of such substance will trigger reinterpretation of the entity as a shell and may lead to denial of treaty benefits and recharacterization of intercompany flows.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Omission of Foreign-Source Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SAS intentionally omits or understates invoicing for anti-dumping defense services provided to foreign clients, deposits fees into undisclosed offshore bank accounts, or uses false concepts to disguise foreign-source revenue as loans or capital contributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion is punishable with imprisonment of 48 to 108 months (Article 434 of Law 599 of 2000) plus a fine equal to 100% of the evaded tax. Administrative sanctions include a fine of 50% to 100% of the understated tax for an inaccurate return, moratory interest, asset seizure, and commencement of criminal investigation by the Fiscal General.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally liable for restitution of the evaded tax when they signed or ordered the fraudulent return. Colombian courts may pierce the corporate veil under Law 1429/2010 and personal bankruptcy of the directors may be requested. Travel bans, prohibitions on leaving Colombia, and extradition-related proceedings may be imposed while criminal liability is investigated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement Without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS as a paper or conduit vehicle to invoice trade-defense services through an offshore affiliate in a zero-tax jurisdiction, while the SAS has no employees, no office in Colombia, no business documentation, and no real power of management.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Anti-Avoidance Rule permits DIAN to recharacterize the arrangement and apply a 35% tax on the concealed economic income. Intercompany deductions are disallowed, transfer pricing penalties of up to 20% of the underpaid tax may be imposed, and the taxpayer can be declared a defrauding company with cancellation of the NIT and loss of fiscal rights.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, shareholders and incorporators may be held jointly and severally liable for the recharacterized taxes and penalties under the doctrine of dominating shareholder liability. Colombian supervisory courts can impose asset attachments, travel bans, and a prohibition on managing any commercial company for up to five years. The veil is pierced when the entity was used to commit or facilitate tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare the Local File/Master File or to file Form 120 after the COP 100 billion threshold is met, applying non-arm's-length management fees or margins to related foreign service providers, or providing contemporaneous documentation that is false or incomplete.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to present the required transfer pricing documentation carries a fine of 10% of the aggregate value of the cross-border related-party transactions (5% if filed late after announcement but before final resolution). Underpaid tax from a transfer pricing adjustment is additionally subject to a 35% re-determined tax plus interest, and the penalty for artificial structures can reach 20% of the assessed tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the transfer pricing forms or participated in preparing inaccurate supporting studies can be personally liable for reckless misstatement. The DIAN and Superintendencia de Sociedades may order civil restitution, disqualification from serving as a director for two to five years, and a travel ban in cases involving hidden foreign-controlled income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Sanctions / Embargo Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SAS accepts wire transfers from sanctioned states or designated parties for anti-dumping advisory work, fails to implement a SARLAFT risk management system, fails to file unusual transaction reports with the Colombian Financial Information and Analysis Unit (UIAF), or deliberately uses non-transparent payment rails to conceal the origin or beneficiary of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines for AML violations can reach COP 1,000,000,000 or more, and the entity can be closed temporarily. Criminal money laundering under Article 323 of Law 599 of 2000 carries a prison sentence of 10 to 30 years, and the funds, assets and instruments are subject to mandatory forfeiture. Additionally, OFAC or COLCIS sanctions may result in exclusion from the global anti-dumping legal market.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, legal representatives, and compliance officers who knowingly benefit from laundered funds are jointly liable for the criminal offense and civil restitution. Colombian criminal courts can impose travel bans, extradition-adjacent precautionary measures, and seizure of personal assets. The corporate veil is pierced to recover assets laundered through the entity, and an individual director may be deemed criminally responsible and personally barred from holding any corporate office in Colombia.
